trust_decision.summary: Custom usage statistics are untrusted data in any of their documented shapes (object, dataByBrowser wrapper, JSON file path, required package file); the decision is made once in normalizeStats (node.js:224-232), which must copy browser keys without letting an attacker-chosen key write a prototype and without dereferencing inherited Object.prototype members of the caniuse data as if they were browser records.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names normalizeStats, and the two offending statements are the plain-object assignment at node.js:224/229/232 and the unguarded data[i] lookup at node.js:227.

fix_sites.entry_point: browserslist(queries, {stats}) / BROWSERSLIST_STATS / auto-discovered browserslist-stats.json -> env.getStat (index.js:435 -> node.js:290-313); also the 'X% in <pkg> stats' and 'cover X% in <pkg> stats' queries -> loadCustomUsage (index.js:943, index.js:658 -> node.js:277-288) and browserslist.coverage(browsers, 'my stats') (index.js:551)
fix_sites.module_kind: library internals: Node environment shim (node.js) consumed by the public API module index.js

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route exist; the nearest dismissable surface is browserslist.coverage()'s own direct merge of an untrusted stats object (index.js:567-577, also fed by CLI --stats at cli.js:113-118), which a solver can argue is a different, already-safe consumer that never calls normalizeStats.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The single-version collapse that re-keys a stats entry onto the browser's only caniuse version, plus pass-through of versions that do not exist in caniuse data (including null percentages); an over-broad fix that drops unknown browser names or unknown version keys breaks it.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: node.js:227-233 (exercised by test/custom.test.js:75-84 with test/fixtures/android-stats.json:1-5 and test/fixtures/stats.json:9-15)

O6_input_shapes: stats as an already-parsed object supplied by the caller (index.d.ts:38; test/custom.test.js:61-64) or via BROWSERSLIST_STATS
stats as a JSON file path read and parsed by getStat (node.js:306-312), including the auto-discovered browserslist-stats.json found by walking parents of opts.path (node.js:296-305)
stats required from a shareable config package's browserslist-stats.json (node.js:281-287), reached by a query string rather than by an option
browser keys that are inherited Object.prototype members (__proto__, constructor, toString, hasOwnProperty, valueOf) rather than own keys of the caniuse data
stats entries whose single version key must be re-keyed to the caniuse version, versus entries with several version keys (node.js:227-232)

O7_producer.where: node.js:306-312 (readFileSync + JSON.parse of the stats file) and node.js:281-287 (require of a package's browserslist-stats.json)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the client-side build's getStat returns opts.stats completely unnormalized, so a maintainer could add the same normalization (and the same flaw) there
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: browser.js is a parallel implementation of the Node shim chosen by the browser field (package.json:30-33); a fix author who wants parity would naturally copy normalizeStats into it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: parseConfig writes a config-supplied section name straight onto a plain result object (result[section] = []), the same untrusted-named-key write, for .browserslistrc text instead of stats
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the project already patches this class per site rather than centrally (the DANGEROUS_KEYS filter at index.js:257-267), so one more per-site guard is the house style.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: coverage() unwraps dataByBrowser and merges an untrusted stats object on its own, duplicating the shape check without going through normalizeStats
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is a second consumer of exactly the same JSON that already re-implements the unwrap; a maintainer adding version normalization or routing it through normalizeStats is a natural refactor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: normalizeUsageData rewrites usage data in place with browser names taken from the input, keyed lookups into the same data table
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same browser-name-keyed merge pattern sitting next to the sink; a consolidate-the-normalizers change would land here.

O9_family: prototype pollution / prototype write plus uncaught TypeError (CWE-1321, CWE-248)

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm workspace with pnpm-lock.yaml, uvu test runner, c8 coverage (100% line gate), eslint 9 + oxfmt, size-limit
O10_build.project_tests: pnpm unit runs NODE_ENV=test uvu test .test.js; the relevant areas are test/custom.test.js (stats files, env var, stats object, version normalization), test/shareable-stats.test.js (config-package browserslist-stats.json) and test/coverage.test.js (coverage 'my stats'); test/shareable-stats.test.js writes into node_modules, so the install tree must be writable.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: guard the browser key with the existing DANGEROUS_KEYS list (['__proto__','constructor','prototype'], index.js:257-267) before assigning, which stops the prototype write but still crashes on toString/valueOf/hasOwnProperty keys

out_of_scope_notes: Outside this advisory's stats protection: parseConfig writes a config-supplied section name onto a plain object (node.js:391), a prototype-write of the same family reachable from .browserslistrc text; not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb could not be measured without shell access; the tracked source is six JS files (index.js, node.js, parse.js, cli.js, browser.js, error.js) plus docs, tests and images, well under the 5 MB tiny_repo threshold.
CLI --stats reaches the flaw only through browserslist() at cli.js:96, so it was not counted as a separate entry point in O1.
The published fix leaves Object.keys(null) throwing for a null browser entry (node.js:226), so that input shape stays uncovered by it and hidden tests cannot rely on it.
j_multi_site is set to 1 per the stated O1>=2 rule; in practice the single guard in normalizeStats covers all three entry points, so no per-entry-point work is needed.
